From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Hart <sophie.hart@brightlane.io>
Date: 2027-05-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Annual deposit burn curve & invoice trigger cadence

Hi Sophie —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As discussed, I sketched a proposal for how we can handle your annual prepay (committed) balance so billing and drawdowns align with your usage pattern and VAT requirements. High level: 

- Annual prepay sits on the ledger and draws down against usage. We propose a monthly trigger check (mid-month) and a top-up invoice when remaining credits drop below 18% of annual balance (configurable).
- For predictable spend months (Q3 product launch), we can schedule phased invoices rather than a single mid-year top-up to smooth GL impact.
- VAT: Redwood will issue invoices showing net value and VAT line; we can send evidence for country-specific reverse-charge where applicable.

What I need from you to finalize:
1) Confirmation you’re comfortable with the 18% trigger (we can change to 20% or a fixed $ threshold).
2) Which legal entity/PO should be on the invoice and whether you need separate country-level VAT lines.
3) If you want staged invoices in July/Aug/Sept for the launch window — pick preferred split (equal or front-loaded).

I’ll loop in our finance ops once you confirm and request a sample invoice and a draft burn-curve workbook for your accounting team.

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0194

Jonas —

Thanks. Quick responses below: 

- 18% seems reasonable but can we cap the top-up at $100k per trigger to avoid large mid-year invoices?
- Our legal entity for Redwood invoices is BrightLane Analytics, Inc. — use PO# BL-PO-7789 when possible.
- VAT: we operate in the US and EU. For EU customers we will need a VAT line per country; we also require an exporter reference for reverse-charge in Germany.
- For the July launch we prefer a front-loaded split: 50% July, 30% Aug, 20% Sept.

Can you send a sample invoice and the burn curve workbook so I can share with Samir and our accounting team? Also include the suggested GL codes for our AP allocation.

Best,
Sophie Hart
